To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression of insulin and of other genes coding for extracellular proteins is modulated in PLN of NOD mice with or without E-IAA and that this early differential expression correlates with the onset of the inflammatory process in the pancreatic islets.
1) the expression of insulin is increased in PLN of 5 weeks NOD mice that will develop diabetes and 2) the expression of genes coding for extracellular proteins is also increased in the same PLN.
the early over expression of messenger RNAs for multiple genes, in the PLN of NOD mice, is associated with islet autoimmunity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel genes implicated in early T1D onset and with the development of novel diagnostic markers and drug targeting strategies.
the early steps of T1D pathogenesis.
the identification of novel targets for early diagnosis and treatment of T1D.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the PLN in NOD mice are a site of early immune activation that is associated with tissue remodelling in the adjacent pancreas, and is a potential source of diagnostic markers and therapeutic targets for T1DM.
the PLN is a tissue undergoing a process of remodelling in NOD mice, and that this process might represent the early steps in T1D pathogenesis.
the immune system is able to recognize tissue damage in the absence of an infectious trigger and to initiate an inflammatory response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the early steps in T1D pathogenesis involve the activation of an immune response directed against a tissue remodelling process, which in the context of the pancreas leads to β cell death.
early over expression of messenger RNAs for multiple genes, in particular insulin and extracellular proteins, is associated with islet autoimmunity.
the PLN of E-IAAs positive mice display an inflammatory state that is not yet detectable by conventional methods, and that is associated with the early steps of T1D development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PLN are a rich source of biomarkers for the early diagnosis and monitoring of the progression of T1D.
the immune system is able to sense and respond to changes in tissue integrity and that this is an important component of early autoimmunity.
a global analysis of gene expression can provide a global view of the disease and generate novel hypothesis concerning its initiation.
